reviewType: independent narrow source and standard test review

sourceReview.independentExpectedModel: Python XS128 Stream imported only from independent oracle; frozen source pool and registration inputs, no production Lua or local runtime card catalog imported
sourceReview.poolOrder: Entire ordered source common/uncommon/rare traversal compared to runtime arrays
sourceReview.spoonBranches: Seed 1 exhausts and generates a Branch card; other four seeds discard; both destinations asserted
sourceReview.drawAssertions: Every wrapper call includes bound or boolean shape, returned value, both complete 64-bit words and counter before/after; phase snapshots and full final hand identities/costs independently checked
sourceReview.rejection: Invalid and stale Discovery selections compare complete combat snapshots and consume no wrapper draws; unrelated permanent and combat random streams are also asserted unchanged
sourceReview.mutation: Temporary module replaces exactly one occurrence of generate(combat,state,p.effect) in Discovery choose; production source is untouched and mutant must fail at discovery_resolve complete stream

limitations: Controlled combat hand/energy/HP/noDraw inputs; not natural acquisition or full PC frame execution
Not all 153 relics or all combinations; broader AC remain outside scope
The existing independent Stream implementation itself is reused, not rewritten or newly authenticated in this review
Source-file SHA literals were checked for preservation and independence, not refetched from the external upstream mirror

resolvedFindings.title: Canonicalize oracle and input hashes or pin their checkout bytes
resolvedFindings.detail: generatorSha256 and inputSha256 hash read_bytes(), while the new oracle and both frozen input JSON files have text/eol attributes unspecified. A Windows core.autocrlf checkout changes these bytes to CRLF. The checked-in fixture retains LF digests, so the standard --check fails oracle fixture drift without any semantic changes. Existing same-project provenance uses explicit LF attributes or normalized UTF-8 text hashes.
resolvedFindings.reproduction: Copied only oracle, Stream dependency, two frozen input files and fixture into an isolated temporary directory, converted LF to CRLF, then ran python3 tools/oracles/sts1_card_random_chain.py --check. Exit 1 with AssertionError: oracle fixture drift. The source worktree was not modified.
resolvedFindings.requestedFix: Normalize all three hashes to canonical LF UTF-8 and regenerate the fixture, or pin all three files with text eol=lf. Add a narrow portability regression or equivalent checkout verification.
resolvedFindings.resolution: All three raw-byte authenticated paths explicitly use text eol=lf. A real Git clone with core.autocrlf=true and core.eol=crlf independently passes strict original oracle regeneration. Unpinned control contains CRLF, all authenticated paths remain LF and byte-equal. No oracle formula, source hash, input, or fixture changes.

checks: Git-created CRLF checkout proved by unpinned control
Original oracle --check succeeds without changed hashes or fixtures
All three pinned paths remain LF and exact-byte-equal
git check-attr confirms text set and eol lf for each path
Reviewed follow-up diff contains only .gitattributes and new checkout regression; no production or oracle/input/fixture changes
portabilityReverification.boundary: Real Git checkout portability exercised on Linux with Windows CRLF settings; not a native Windows runtime execution. No full suite repeated.
